channel.title: AeroSpork
channel.description: Updates for AeroSpork, an i3-like tiling window manager for macOS.

item.description:
Fixes workspace memory doing nothing after a reboot, a case where editing a window rule could damage unrelated parts of your config, and the missing licence in every previous download.

Workspace memory now works on a cold boot

1.1.5 remembered which workspace each window was on, but at login it forgot any application that had not finished starting. AeroSpork launches alongside every other login item and macOS's own window restore, so a slow app was absent from the first snapshot — and that snapshot was written straight over the memory, deleting its entry before the app ever appeared.

So the case the feature exists for, restarting your Mac, was the one it skipped. It now waits for those windows instead of forgetting them.

Also fixed: if a logout was cancelled by another app, AeroSpork kept running with its memory frozen and never saved again for the rest of the session.

Editing a window rule could damage unrelated config

Three ways, all fixed:

  • A regex containing [ — an ordinary thing to write in a window-title matcher — silently

switched off every safety check for the rest of the file. Those checks are what stop the editor rewriting things it cannot represent, including a monitor pinned by hardware fingerprint, so an edit elsewhere could quietly degrade it to a plain name.

  • A comment after a section header, like [on-window] # my rules, made that section

unrecognisable to the writer. It added a second copy instead of replacing it, so every rule in the table applied twice.

  • A monitor written as a list of fallbacks was reduced to its first entry — including on rows you

did not touch, since one edit rewrites the whole section. It is now refused with a pointer to the Raw TOML tab rather than silently truncated.

The licence was missing from every download

legal/LICENSE.txt was a link to a file that was never included in the archive, so every release shipped the four third-party licences and not AeroSpork's own. The release now carries it, and the packaging refuses to build an archive with a broken link in it.

Update notes and the state file

The Check for Updates dialog showed a blank "what's new" pane. It now shows these notes.

Workspace memory moved from /tmp to ~/Library/Caches/com.wbs.aerospork/workspace-memory.json and is readable only by you. It lists which applications are running and which monitors are attached, which no other account on the machine needs to see, and /tmp is writable by anyone — a file planted there decided where your windows went. Upgrading leaves the old file behind; it is ignored and safe to delete.

Universal (arm64 + x86_64), signed with a Developer ID, notarized and stapled.

Install

brew install --cask wbsmolen/tap/aerospork

Or download aerospork-v1.1.6.zip, move aerospork-v1.1.6/AeroSpork.app to /Applications, and grant Accessibility permission when prompted. Optionally put aerospork-v1.1.6/bin/aerospork on your PATH for the CLI.

AeroSpork-1.1.6.zip is the Sparkle update archive — the same app without the CLI, man pages or licence files. It exists for the updater; prefer the versioned zip for a manual install.
